The first conversation

What a project consultation covers

The first conversation is not a quote window.

Request a consultation Explore kitchen design ideas

RT Signature Homes uses a project consultation to see whether the property, the scope, and the way we work are a fit. Complex residential work needs information about existing conditions, access, selections, and timing before anyone should name a responsible number.

That is the offer. It is not a remodel planner form, and it is not a race against three GC bids.

What we are trying to learn

  • Where the house is, and who has jurisdiction for permits
  • What you want the project to make possible (kitchen, bath, ADU, whole-home, or something else)
  • What is already true on site (age, prior work, access, whether you will live there during construction)
  • Priorities: function, timing, and how much of the house is in play
  • Whether the job is a qualifying project for a Redmond design-build team

We take qualifying work across Washington. The office is in Redmond at 4164 148th Ave NE. Other communities are service areas. Check Google Maps for the current rating and customer feedback. The first conversation starts with your house.

What you can prepare

You do not need a full drawing set. Useful context:

  • Address and a few photos of the rooms in play
  • How you use the house now
  • Any survey, prior permit, or HOA rule you already have
  • Timing constraints (events, occupancy, school year)
  • Whether this is one room or a sequence of rooms

Optional investment ranges exist on the contact form as a planning aid. They are not a bid.

Prefer to talk now? Call (206) 407-6291.

What we will not do on that first call

  • Invent a guaranteed price, schedule, or permit outcome
  • Treat design-gallery photography as a finished version of your future house
  • Pretend a city we have not discussed against your address is already a scoped project

After the conversation

If it is not a fit, we should say so. If it is, the next step is more investigation, not demolition. That may include a site visit, clarifying scope, and only then talking about how design, permitting, and construction would be sequenced.

Related reading: Design-build vs. a general contractor and How to pick a licensed remodeler in Washington.

If the work is a Seattle or Eastside kitchen, bath, or ADU, these pages describe the scope:

  • Kitchen remodeling in Seattle and the Eastside
  • Bathroom remodeling in Seattle and the Eastside
  • ADU builder in Seattle and the Eastside

Questions homeowners ask

Will the first conversation provide an instant project price?

Complex residential work requires information about the property, existing conditions, scope, selections, access, and schedule before a responsible recommendation can be made.

When should I request a consultation?

Reach out while you are defining the scope, priorities, investment expectations, and timing. Early context makes the first project conversation more useful.

What kinds of projects are a fit?

The team evaluates qualifying Washington residential projects including whole-home remodeling, kitchens, bathrooms, additions, ADUs, custom homes, exterior improvements, flooring, and painting.

Do I have to fill out every optional field?

No. Start with the essentials on the consultation form. Photos and plans help but are not required for the first conversation.
